solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Robot old lady hit gets irate ultimately

parts.note: MA is an informal word for mother, one's old lady
to chin someone is to punch them on the jaw

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word irate

explanation.surface: An elderly woman lashes out and grows furious in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chin' as a verb is British slang for punching someone on the jaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot is an automated device, a mechanical contraption doing work by itself.

clue.text: Extremely small parent's lowest point

parts.note: mini means very small
mum is a mother, a parent

explanation.surface: A tiny parent hits rock bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The minimum is the least amount or bottom level something reaches.

clue.text: Vegetable that goes with premium ginger

parts.note: a carrot is a vegetable
top means best or premium, as in top quality

explanation.surface: A vegetable that pairs well with high-quality ginger in a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ginger' looks like the spice, but is a red-haired person.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrot-top is an informal nickname for a red-haired person, as is ginger.

clue.text: English player seen in press with Scottish leader

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them

indicators.note: leader indicates the first letter of Scottish

explanation.surface: An English footballer appears in the newspapers alongside a Scottish boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' suggests sport; it is an actor, Jeremy Irons.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Irons is a well-known English actor, a stage and screen performer.

clue.text: Passionate online movement a failure essentially

parts.note: E is short for electronic, used for things online
a motion is a movement

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core, the middle letter of failure

explanation.surface: A heated internet campaign which fundamentally flopped.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone emotional is easily stirred by strong feeling, as a fervent person is.

clue.text: Nipper bro let off, admitting first of sins

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so one piece goes inside the other
off suggests the letters of bro let have gone wrong and need rearranging
first of picks the opening letter of sins

explanation.surface: A brother is excused even though he confesses to a misdeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges BROLET to LOBTER, and 'admitting' takes the S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobster has pincers that nip, so it is jokingly a nipper.

clue.text: Move like a snake shedding skin that's supple

indicators.note: shedding skin means removing the outer letters, as a snake sheds its skin

parts.note: to slither is to move like a snake

explanation.surface: A snake slides along after casting its skin, and is flexible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shedding skin' drops the outer letters S and R of SLITHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means flexible and graceful, bending easily.

clue.text: A butcher about to steal shilling in foreign capital

indicators.note: stealing means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other
about here means moved around, so the letters of a butcher are rearranged

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for shilling, an old British coin

explanation.surface: A meat seller is set to pocket a coin while abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges ABUTCHER to BUCHARET, and 'to steal' takes S inside. A shilling was a pre-1971 British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucharest is the capital city of Romania.

clue.text: Tense German must leave rank occupation

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: leave means go away from, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: a grade is a rank

explanation.surface: An anxious German has to quit the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must leave' takes G out of GRADE, giving RADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade is a line of work, a job or craft.

clue.text: Career that's consuming Dutch novelist

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to career is to rush headlong
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A profession that devours a writer from the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a job but is the verb to hurtle; RUSH and IE together 'consume' D.
explanation.definitionFit: Salman Rushdie is a famous author of novels such as Midnight's Children.

clue.text: Drug smuggler in Orange County fled to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: OC is the standard abbreviation for Orange County, California
fled means ran away

explanation.surface: A trafficker based in southern California escaped westwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Narco is a slang shortening of narcotics trafficker, a dealer in illegal drugs.

clue.text: They might help you see captions I redesigned

indicators.note: redesigned says the letters of captions I are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone has reworked the captions, perhaps to make them easier to read.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye specialists test sight and prescribe glasses, helping people with their vision.

clue.text: Medical officer addicted to Polish liquor

parts.note: to be on a drug is to be hooked on it
to polish shoes is to shine them

explanation.surface: A military doctor hooked on Polish vodka.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the verb meaning buff up.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine is illicitly distilled spirit, a kind of homemade hard drink.

clue.text: Chaps must split bill? That's correct!

indicators.note: splitting a word means pushing something into its middle, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: AD is short for advertisement, a bill or poster
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Some men insist on dividing the restaurant bill, and someone agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to correct or revise, typically a text or law.

clue.text: Having been struck, one will become inflamed

definitions.text: Having been struck, one will become inflamed

parts.words: Having been struck, one will become inflamed
parts.note: reads like someone hit and getting angry or swollen, but describes a lit stick for making fire

explanation.surface: Someone who has been hit will get angry or sore.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is struck against a rough strip and bursts into flame.

clue.text: One who mesmerises writhing python is on time

indicators.note: writhing means twisting about, so the letters of python are rearranged

explanation.surface: A snake charmer's python squirms when it is time.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypnotist puts people into a trance, mesmerising them.

clue.text: Hit the person in charge of an organisation

definitions.text: the person in charge of an organisation
definitions.meaning: ... also means the boss, the top person

explanation.surface: Someone has struck the company boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are about being top: the best-selling single and the chief.

clue.text: Moralist gets upset by bit of nooky and this?

definitions.text: Moralist gets upset by bit of nooky and this?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of moralist are rearranged
bit of picks the first letter of nooky

explanation.surface: A prude is offended by some sex, which they consider a grave sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets upset' rearranges MORALIST to MORTALSI. The whole clue also describes what a moralist might call a bit of nooky.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortal sin is a grave wrong; a moralist might so label casual sex.

clue.text: Exactly where a fielder might put sunscreen?

definitions.text: where a fielder might put sunscreen?
definitions.meaning: a cricket fielder in the sun would apply cream ...

explanation.surface: A sunny cricket match, and the precise spot for applying protection.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom on the nose means precisely right; literally it is a place on the face.

clue.text: A French tree seen around uni lacking admirers?

parts.note: UN is the French for a

indicators.note: seen around means one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a poplar is a tree
U is short for university, uni

explanation.surface: A French tree growing round a university campus, apparently ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unpopular has few fans; the query flags that the phrase describes rather than defines.

clue.text: You might say Bob on a drop of retsina gets hazy

parts.note: the British phrase Bob's your uncle, meaning there you go, links Bob with uncle

indicators.note: drop of picks the first letter of retsina

explanation.surface: Bob is nodding off after a little Greek wine and gets fuzzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob's your uncle' is a British expression meaning 'and that's that'. 'on' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unclear is vague or fuzzy, not easily understood.

clue.text: Encountered books written about a symbolic item

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the letters are written backwards

parts.note: encountered means met
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone came across books on a symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or emblem treated as a sacred symbol of a clan.

clue.text: One lad supporting Trump-like president

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed beneath

parts.note: mad, crazy, as the setter suggests of Trump
I is the Roman numeral one
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: One young man backs a president in the Trump mould.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, I and SON go below MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: James Madison was the fourth President of the United States.

clue.text: Conservative embarrassed by old principles

definitions.note: a credo is one word for a whole set of principles

parts.note: embarrassed people go red

explanation.surface: A Tory is shamed by his outdated values.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of beliefs, a body of guiding tenets.

clue.text: Message European man via a mobile phone

indicators.note: heard over the phone means the word is spoken, so we go by its sound

parts.note: a man is a male

explanation.surface: Contact a man from Europe using a mobile.
explanation.definitionFit: An email is an electronic message, sent between computers.

clue.text: Support protecting liberal principal in a spot

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping around, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to back is to support
a principal is a head of a school

explanation.surface: Backing a Liberal headteacher who is in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a spot' looks like trouble, but means a pimple.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackhead is a pimple, a small dark blocked pore on the skin.

clue.text: In the sack, engineers might do this

definitions.text: In the sack, engineers might do this

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Engineers in bed might reproduce.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps; the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To breed is to reproduce, which couples might do in bed.

clue.text: Religious work fine to be put up by artist and knight

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means raised so the word fine's synonym reads bottom to top

parts.note: OK means fine
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A fine that a painter and a knight must pay over a sacred text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be put up' turns OK into KO, read upwards in this down answer; 'by' joins it to RA and N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Koran is the holy book of Islam.

clue.text: Old American pit workers can be testing folk

parts.note: EX means former or old
A is a short abbreviation for American
miners work in a pit

explanation.surface: Former American coal miners can be trying people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'testing' looks like annoying, but means setting tests.
explanation.definitionFit: Examiners are people who set and mark exams, so they test others.

clue.text: Public disturbances can be hugely fun occasions

definitions.meaning: a riot is also informally a hilarious time

explanation.surface: Street unrest can turn out to be great fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Riots are violent mob outbreaks; colloquially, a riot is a highly entertaining event.

clue.text: Behind-pinching socialist will get reported

indicators.note: pinching means gripping, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: a red is a socialist or left-winger
behind schedule means late

explanation.surface: A left-winger who pinches a bottom will be reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind-pinching' suggests groping, but 'Behind' is LATE and 'pinching' the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell or recount it, as a reporter does.

clue.text: Old relative eager to get a durable fabric

parts.note: nan is a grandmother, an older relative
keen means eager

explanation.surface: Granny is keen to buy some hardwearing cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a sturdy yellowish cotton cloth, originally from Nanjing.
